title: Section 6: Independence, Assistive Technology & Life After Injury
source_document: English Master Data Collection & Clinical Content Repository

content.text: Living with a spinal cord injury involves adapting daily routines, returning to personal roles, and engaging fully in social and professional life:

items: Daily Living & Autonomy: Developing confidence in problem-solving, self-advocacy, and directing personal care assistance.
Education & Employment: Vocational rehabilitation, workplace accommodations, adaptive computer access, and flexible schedules support career continuation or retraining.
Rights & Equal Access: Understanding disability rights, accessibility legislation, and advocacy resources to promote barrier-free public environments.
Leisure & Adaptive Sports: Participation in adapted recreation, community organizations, and peer networks enhances physical fitness and social wellbeing.

content.text: Selecting appropriate assistive equipment enhances safety and functional independence:

items: Mobility Devices: Manual wheelchairs (ultra-lightweight, folding, or rigid) and power wheelchairs customized with pressure-relieving seating cushions (air, gel, or foam combination).
Transfer Aids: Transfer boards, swivel seats, and mechanical patient lifts to facilitate safe transitions.
Orthoses & Walking Aids: Ankle-Foot Orthoses (AFOs), Knee-Ankle-Foot Orthoses (KAFOs), walkers, or crutches prescribed for standing and ambulation.
Environmental Control Technologies: Smart home voice controls, modified door openers, and adaptive device interfaces.
